description: FIND-005 identified that no REQ specifies how discord_user_id is obtained for the cancel flow. The cancel endpoint needs discord_user_id to acquire the advisory lock (REQ-BILL-004) and look up the member. REQ-BILL-002 describes link session validation returning a record but does not explicitly state that the record contains discord_user_id. The effectful shell function validateLinkSession (behavioral-spec.md line 43) returns LinkSessionRecord but this type is not defined, so an implementer cannot confirm it includes discord_user_id. The subscribe flow uses consumeLinkSession (line 42) which is also underspecified. This finding was NOT listed in the fixesSummary and remains unresolved. While the purity boundary section implicitly assumes discord_user_id flows from the link session, the REQs themselves do not make this explicit for the cancel path.

evidence.snippet:
consumeLinkSession(db, tokenHash): Promise<LinkSessionRecord | null>
validateLinkSession(db, tokenHash): Promise<LinkSessionRecord | null>

sourceReference.snippet: discord_link_sessions: link_session_token_hash (text, unique), discord_user_id (text), expires_at, used_at

remediation: Add a note to REQ-BILL-002 or a dedicated REQ clarifying that LinkSessionRecord includes discord_user_id, and that both the subscribe and cancel flows obtain discord_user_id from the link session. This is implementation-critical because advisory lock acquisition depends on it.
